title: MDOT pauses lane closures Wednesday afternoon as rain moves into Pontotoc County
excerpt: Wednesday’s rain chance is near 100% in Pontotoc County. Most new highway lane closures pause Wednesday afternoon through Monday morning.
locality: Pontotoc County, Mississippi, in NWS zone MSZ015. MDOT closure policy applies statewide.

facts.statement: Mississippi highway crews will pause nonemergency lane closures Wednesday afternoon, just as Pontotoc County heads into its wettest travel day of Thanksgiving week. The pause runs through Monday morning, Nov. 30. Drivers can still encounter lanes that were already closed for safety, including at work sites where crews have gone home.
facts.evidence: MDOT gives statewide start and end periods and explains continuing protective closures. NWS local bulletin gives Wednesday the highest rain probability through the holiday weekend.

facts.locality: Pontotoc County, Mississippi, in NWS zone MSZ015. MDOT closure policy applies statewide.
facts.identities: Mississippi Department of Transportation and National Weather Service Memphis.

The daytime high is expected to reach only the lower 50s. The rain chance falls to 50% Wednesday evening.

paragraphs.text: Mississippi highway crews will pause nonemergency lane closures Wednesday afternoon, just as Pontotoc County heads into its wettest travel day of Thanksgiving week. The pause runs through Monday morning, Nov. 30. Drivers can still encounter lanes that were already closed for safety, including at work sites where crews have gone home.

For travelers leaving Pontotoc early, the rain could arrive before the work stops. The National Weather Service’s 3:05 p.m. Tuesday forecast gives the county a 70% chance of rain after midnight and a near-100% chance Wednesday. The daytime high is expected to reach only the lower 50s. The rain chance falls to 50% Wednesday evening.

Thanksgiving Day should turn mostly sunny after a cloudy morning, but northwest winds could gust to 25 mph. The forecast high is in the mid-40s, followed by a low around 30 Thursday night. Friday is expected to be sunny with a high in the mid-50s. For the return trip Sunday, the weather service puts the chance of showers at 50%.

MDOT asks drivers to treat any remaining lane closures as active work zones. Before leaving, drivers can check their route on the free MDOT Traffic app or the agency’s traffic map for current conditions and cameras.
